answer: Admission requires 1,000 units of fresh computational work per identity to act as a lotus bloom, where each task result functions as a unique prism of effort. The verifier scans the pigment of every incoming solution against a ledger of past work to block duplicates. An honest participant pays this base cost, but an attacker spawning 1,000 fakes faces 1,000,000 puzzles. Failure triggers an immediate identity burn.
